findings.subject: Templo Mayor Discover opening evidence
findings.assertion: 1428 is the standard shorthand for a Triple Alliance of Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan, but its political formation around the Tepanec war should be presented as a process, not an uncontested single-day event.
evidence_locators: Centro de México; Los últimos en llegar
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Check Chimalpahin, Barlow, Santamarina and Tlacopan entry chronology before exact founding language

findings.subject: Templo Mayor Discover opening evidence
findings.assertion: The Templo Mayor was enlarged repeatedly; its two principal shrines were Tláloc on the north and Huitzilopochtli on the south.
evidence_locators: Templo Mayor; seven enlargements and two stairways
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Observe separate north/south stairways and nested building phases

findings.subject: Templo Mayor Discover opening evidence
findings.assertion: López Luján describes a dismembered Coyolxauhqui relief from stage IVa-1, earlier than the better-known monolithic disk associated with stage IVb, occupying a corresponding position beneath the southern shrine.
evidence_locators: Las otras imágenes de Coyolxauhqui; IVa-1 and IVb discussion; printed publication pp.48–54 not directly inspected
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Original 1978 and 1987 field reports remain to be examined

findings.subject: Templo Mayor Discover opening evidence
findings.assertion: The Coyolxauhqui stone uncovered in February 1978 prompted the archaeological project, while the interpretive connection to the Coatepec story depends on iconography and ritual contextual arguments.
evidence_locators: Proyecto Templo Mayor; discovery and founding paragraphs
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Do not present a specific sacrifice enactment as direct archaeological observation

findings.subject: Templo Mayor Discover opening evidence
findings.assertion: INAH reports destruction of the Templo Mayor following the defeat of 13 August 1521, with colonial houses erected over its former site. Surviving lower stages are not the intact exterior seen in 1519.
evidence_locators: La Conquista; ¿Qué ocurrió con el Templo Mayor?
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Precise demolitions and property chronology need archival documentation

findings.subject: Templo Mayor Discover opening evidence
findings.assertion: INAH identifies an approximately 1900 brick water collector under the modern walkway, with a trench cutting through the ancient temple construction stages across a strip about two metres wide.
evidence_locators: Etapa IV y V; Colector de agua
findings.remaining_uncertainty: On-site: look at the collector and changed archaeological fabric

findings.subject: Templo Mayor Discover opening evidence
findings.assertion: INAH dates discovery by electric-company workers of Coyolxauhqui to 21 February 1978 and names Eduardo Matos Moctezuma as founder of Proyecto Templo Mayor.
evidence_locators: Proyecto Templo Mayor, opening and team-history paragraphs
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Project inception is not the first investigation of this location

findings.subject: Templo Mayor Discover opening evidence
findings.assertion: INAH credits Manuel Gamio with uncovering the southwest temple corner in 1914; its English guide dates the site museum opening to 12 October 1987. The 1978 find was not the first archaeological indication of the Templo Mayor.
evidence_locators: Templo Mayor English history; Gamio and museum opening passages
